card.title: Work-energy theorem — the ledger that solves motion

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Work is force delivered along displacement (W = F·s·cosθ). Whatever net work flows into a body appears as kinetic energy — that is the theorem. Conservative forces (gravity, spring) store work as recoverable potential energy, so mechanical energy is conserved in their world; friction spends it as heat, permanently.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: W = F·s·cosθ (variable force: ∫F·ds)  ·  KE = ½mv², gravitational PE = mgh, elastic PE = ½kx²  ·  W_net = ΔKE  ·  P = W/t = F·v, 1 HP = 746 W, 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ  ·  elastic collision: momentum + KE both conserved

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The theorem uses NET work — every force counts, including friction. Mechanical-energy conservation additionally demands no non-conservative work. 'Elastic collision' means kinetic energy survives the impact (ideal atomic-scale truth, macroscopic approximation).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Zero work: force perpendicular to motion (centripetal force, carrying a load horizontally). Negative work: friction and brakes drain the ledger. Head-on elastic collision of equal masses swaps velocities. Motor lifting 500 kg through 20 m at 2 kW: t = mgh/P = 100 s (NEB 2022).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 4 kg released from rest, falls 10 m (g = 9.8): lost PE = gained KE → KE = mgh = 4 × 9.8 × 10 = 392 J at impact (NEB 2023, 4 marks). No kinematics needed — the energy ledger jumps straight from height to speed.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The ledger tracks mechanical energy only: work against friction exits as heat and the theorem will not return it. Perfectly elastic macroscopic collisions do not exist (sound + deformation always tax the impact). Average power (W/t) hides the instantaneous story P = F·v.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Constant force proof (the NEB 5-marker): W = F·s with s = (v²−u²)/2a and F = ma → W = ma·(v²−u²)/2a = ½mv² − ½mu² = ΔKE. For variable force the same steps run under an integral, W = ∫F·dx — the area under the F–x graph.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: When time and path look messy, abandon kinematics for the energy ledger: write mgh + ½mv² + ½kx² at start and end, equate (minus friction loss). Height ↔ speed conversions collapse to v = √(2gh). Collisions: try momentum first, add KE-conservation only if 'elastic' is stated.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (5): state and prove the work-energy theorem for a constant force. NEB 2022 (3): 2 kW motor lifts 500 kg through 20 m — time taken. NEB 2022 (3): 60 kg person climbs 8 m in 20 s — power developed.
